text.en: Raju saw a fossil of a shell in a museum. "That shows life of long ago," said his teacher.

Life on Earth began about 3.5 to 4 billion years ago. Evidences for evolution come from fossils, comparative anatomy and embryology. Lamarck's theory said that organs used more are developed and passed on, while Darwin's theory of natural selection said that the fittest organisms in a changing environment survive.
Variation is the difference among individuals of the same species, and it is the raw material for natural selection. Palaeobotany is the study of fossil plants, and fossilisation is how remains are preserved in rocks, whose age can be found by radioactive dating.
Ethnobotany studies how people use plants, and astrobiology or exobiology looks for life beyond Earth.
